bib.title: Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch), chapter 3: Coding attention mechanisms

question: How do you code, step by step in PyTorch, the self-attention mechanism of a GPT-like LLM, from simplified attention to causal multi-head attention?
contributions: Scaled dot-product self-attention with trainable query, key and value matrices
Causal attention with a mask and dropout
Multi-head attention as a wrapper over causal heads and as an efficient weight-split class

limits: Toy sizes only (d_in=3, d_out=2, 6 tokens) to keep outputs readable; the author says so for the multi-head class.
No timing or memory measurements: the efficiency claim for the weight-split MultiHeadAttention over the wrapper is argued, not measured.
No training in this chapter; weights are random (requires_grad=False).
practices: Use softmax for normalising attention scores, not the naive version, because of overflow and underflow (3.3.1).
Divide scores by sqrt of key dimension before softmax to avoid small gradients (3.4.1).
Prefer nn.Linear over nn.Parameter(torch.rand) for projections because of its better weight initialisation (3.4.2).
Mask scores with -inf before softmax instead of masking and renormalising (3.5.1).
Apply dropout to attention weights after softmax, only during training (3.5.2).
Use register_buffer for the mask so it moves with the model across devices (3.5.3).
Compute heads with one projection and a view/transpose split rather than a list of separate heads (3.6.2).

terms.definition: a mechanism that allows each position in the input sequence to consider the relevancy of, or "attend to," all other positions in the same sequence when computing the representation of a sequence
can be interpreted as an enriched embedding vector
also known as masked attention; restricts a model to only consider previous and current inputs in a sequence when processing any given token
self-attention with trainable query, key and value matrices where scores are divided by the square root of the key embedding dimension
